### workspace work-queue --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace work-queue add workflow ID [--ref REF] [--prompt TEXT] [--input K=V]... [OPTIONS]
       workspace work-queue add go ARG [--text] [--workflow ID] [--input K=V]... [OPTIONS]
       workspace work-queue list [--name WORKSPACE | --project [NAME]] [--json]
       workspace work-queue show ITEM [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace work-queue active [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace work-queue rm ITEM... [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace work-queue move ITEM (--before ID | --after ID | --top | --bottom) [--if-revision N] [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace work-queue cancel [ITEM] [--and-continue] [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace work-queue enable [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace work-queue disable [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace work-queue resume [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace work-queue skip [ITEM] [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace work-queue advance [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace work-queue status [--name WORKSPACE | --project [NAME]] [--json]
       workspace work-queue history list [--since DATE] [--before DATE] [--state STATE] [--name WORKSPACE | --project [NAME]] [--json]
       workspace work-queue history show ITEM [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace work-queue history clear (--before DATE | --all) [--yes] [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]

Each workspace has its own queue of items that run one at a time (`wq` is another name for
`work-queue`). A queue is off until `work-queue enable`. Only `work-queue advance` moves it, one
pass by hand, so run it again after each item ends.

Subcommands:
  add            Add an item to the end of a workspace's queue
  list           Show the queue as a table
  show           Show one queued item in full
  active         Show the item that is running and what it waits on
  rm             Remove queued items
  move           Move a queued item
  cancel         Cancel the running item and pause the queue
  enable         Turn the workspace's queue on
  disable        Turn the workspace's queue off
  resume         Clear the queue's pause
  skip           Skip the held item and clear the pause
  advance        Run one pass of the queue by hand
  status         Show one line per queue: on or off, pause, active item
  history list   List finished items, oldest first
  history show   Show one finished item with its spec
  history clear  Delete finished items
Run `workspace work-queue VERB --help` for a verb's options.

        --name NAME                  Workspace whose queue to use (default: detected from the current directory)
        --project [NAME]             list, status and history list: every workspace of a project (read only)
        --top                        add: put the item first among the queued ones; move: move it there
        --bottom                     move: move the item to the end
        --after-current              add: put the item right after the one that is running
        --before VALUE               add and move: place the item before this item id; history list and clear: finished before this date
        --after ID                   add and move: place the item after this item id
        --if-revision N              move: refuse with stale_revision unless the queue's revision is N
        --headless                   add: run the item without a pane
        --on-fail MODE               add: stop (pause the queue when it fails, the default) or continue
        --dedupe-key KEY             add: adding the same key again changes nothing
        --ref REF                    add workflow: the ticket, pull request or branch to start from
        --prompt TEXT                add workflow: the task text
        --input K=V                  add: a workflow input (repeatable)
        --text                       add go: ARG is free text, not a ticket, pull request or branch
        --workflow ID                add go: the workflow to run instead of the one config picks
        --and-continue               cancel: go on to the next item instead of pausing the queue
        --since DATE                 history list: finished at or after this date (2026-01-31 or 2026-01-31T09:00:00Z)
        --state STATE                history list: only this outcome (succeeded, failed, cancelled, skipped, interrupted, launch_failed)
        --all                        history clear: remove every finished item
        --yes                        history clear: skip the question
        --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                       Show this help

Examples:
  workspace work-queue add workflow rpiv --prompt "Add SSO login"    # queue an rpiv run for that task
  workspace work-queue list    # the queue of the workspace you are in
  workspace work-queue show 3fa9    # one item by the start of its id
  workspace work-queue active    # which item the queue is on, and what it waits for
  workspace work-queue rm 3fa9    # drop one queued item
  workspace work-queue move 3fa9 --top    # run this one next
  workspace work-queue cancel    # stop the running item and hold the queue
  workspace work-queue enable    # turn the queue on, then run `workspace work-queue advance`
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace work-queue add --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace work-queue add workflow ID [--ref REF] [--prompt TEXT] [--input K=V]... [OPTIONS]
       workspace work-queue add go ARG [--text] [--workflow ID] [--input K=V]... [OPTIONS]

Add an item to the end of a workspace's queue.

A `workflow` item starts a workflow run in the workspace's checkout; a `go` item runs `workspace go
--here` there. It prints the item's id and position. Give at most one of --top, --after-current, --before and --after.
The queue runs items only once it is on (`workspace work-queue enable`). Adding the same --dedupe-key
again changes nothing and says `unchanged`. Anything but `workflow` or `go` is a usage error.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)
    --top                        Put the item first among the queued ones
    --after-current              Put the item right after the one that is running
    --before ID                  Put the item before this item
    --after ID                   Put the item after this item
    --headless                   Run the item without a pane
    --on-fail MODE               stop (pause the queue when it fails, the default) or continue
    --dedupe-key KEY             Adding the same key again changes nothing
    --ref REF                    workflow: the ticket, pull request or branch to start from
    --prompt TEXT                workflow: the task text
    --input K=V                  A workflow input (repeatable)
    --text                       go: ARG is free text, not a ticket, pull request or branch
    --workflow ID                go: the workflow to run instead of the one config picks
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace work-queue add workflow rpiv --prompt "Add SSO login"    # queue an rpiv run for that task
  workspace work-queue add workflow pr-feedback --ref 123    # queue a workflow for pull request 123
  workspace work-queue add go PROJ-42 --top    # queue `go` for a ticket and run it before the others
  workspace work-queue add go --text "Fix the flaky login spec" --on-fail continue    # queue free text; a failure does not pause the queue
  workspace work-queue add go PROJ-43 --dedupe-key PROJ-43 --json    # for a script: adding it twice answers `unchanged`
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace work-queue list --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace work-queue list [--name WORKSPACE | --project [NAME]] [--json]

Show the queue as a table.

One row per item: position, id, state, kind, what it runs, headless and age. A footer says whether the
queue is on, off or paused (and why); an off queue says how to turn it on. --project reads every
workspace of a project and writes nothing.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)
    --project [NAME]             Every workspace of a project (NAME, or the project of the current workspace), read only
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace work-queue list    # the queue of the workspace you are in
  workspace work-queue list --project    # every queue of the project, to see which one is stuck
  workspace work-queue list --name api.worktree-x --json    # one JSON document, with the revision that --if-revision takes
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace work-queue show --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace work-queue show ITEM [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]

Show one queued item in full.

ITEM is an item id or a unique start of one (see `workspace work-queue list`).
It prints the item's spec, state, run and log path. A finished item is in `work-queue history show`.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace work-queue show 3fa9    # one item by the start of its id
  workspace work-queue show 3fa9 --name api.worktree-x    # the same in another workspace
  workspace work-queue show 3fa9 --json    # one JSON document, with next actions

--- end

### workspace work-queue active --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace work-queue active [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]

Show the item that is running and what it waits on.

Says `Nothing is active` when no item is starting, active or held. A held item waits on a person; its next actions say how to approve or skip.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace work-queue active    # which item the queue is on, and what it waits for
  workspace work-queue active --name api.worktree-x    # the same for another workspace
  workspace work-queue active --json    # one JSON document, for a script
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace work-queue rm --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace work-queue rm ITEM... [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]

Remove queued items.

ITEM is an item id or a unique start of one (see `workspace work-queue list`).
All or none: a name that matches no item, or two, removes nothing. The running item refuses with item_active; use `work-queue cancel`.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace work-queue rm 3fa9    # drop one queued item
  workspace work-queue rm 3fa9 b71c    # drop two at once
  workspace work-queue rm 3fa9 --json    # for a script: one result row per item removed
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace work-queue move --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace work-queue move ITEM (--before ID | --after ID | --top | --bottom) [--if-revision N] [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]

Move a queued item.

ITEM is an item id or a unique start of one (see `workspace work-queue list`).
Give exactly one of --before, --after, --top and --bottom. The running item can't move. Moving an item to where it is says `unchanged`.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)
    --before ID                  Put the item before this item
    --after ID                   Put the item after this item
    --top                        Put the item first among the queued ones
    --bottom                     Put the item last
    --if-revision N              Refuse with stale_revision unless the queue's revision is N
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace work-queue move 3fa9 --top    # run this one next
  workspace work-queue move 3fa9 --after b71c    # place it behind another item
  workspace work-queue move 3fa9 --bottom --if-revision 12    # only if nobody changed the queue since you read revision 12
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace work-queue cancel --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace work-queue cancel [ITEM] [--and-continue] [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]

Cancel the running item and pause the queue.

With no ITEM it is the item that is starting, active or held. Its workflow run is cancelled and the item
goes to history as `cancelled`; the queue pauses until `work-queue resume`. With --and-continue it does not
pause, and one pass starts the next item. A queued item is removed with `work-queue rm`.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)
    --and-continue               Go on to the next item instead of pausing the queue
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace work-queue cancel    # stop the running item and hold the queue
  workspace work-queue cancel --and-continue    # stop it and start the next one
  workspace work-queue cancel 3fa9 --json    # for a script: the cancelled item's row
--- stderr
--- end

--- stdout

Its workflow run is cancelled and the item\ngoes to history as `cancelled`; the queue pauses until `work-queue resume`. With --and-continue it does not\npause, and one pass starts the next item. A queued item is removed with `work-queue rm`.","options":[{"flags":"--name NAME","description":"Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)"},{"flags":"--and-continue","description":"Go on to the next item instead of pausing the queue"},{"flags":"--json","description":"Print one JSON document"},{"flags":"-h, --help","description":"Show this help"}],"examples":[{"command":"workspace work-queue cancel","scenario":"stop the running item and hold the queue"},{"command":"workspace work-queue cancel --and-continue","scenario":"stop it and start the next one"},{"command":"workspace work-queue cancel 3fa9 --json","scenario":"for a script: the cancelled item's row"}]}

### workspace work-queue enable --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace work-queue enable [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]

Turn the workspace's queue on.

A queue is off until it is enabled; `work-queue add` alone does not run anything. Enable it, then
`work-queue advance` runs one pass by hand. The setting is kept in the queue file; with none set,
config `work_queue.enabled` applies.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace work-queue enable    # turn the queue on, then run `workspace work-queue advance`
  workspace work-queue enable --name api.worktree-x    # turn on another workspace's queue
  workspace work-queue enable --json    # one JSON document: `enabled` or `unchanged`
--- stderr
--- end

--- exit 0
--- stdout

Enable it, then\n`work-queue advance` runs one pass by hand. The setting is kept in the queue file; with none set,\nconfig `work_queue.enabled` applies.","options":[{"flags":"--name NAME","description":"Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)"},{"flags":"--json","description":"Print one JSON document"},{"flags":"-h, --help","description":"Show this help"}],"examples":[{"command":"workspace work-queue enable","scenario":"turn the queue on, then run `workspace work-queue advance`"},{"command":"workspace work-queue enable --name api.worktree-x","scenario":"turn on another workspace's queue"},{"command":"workspace work-queue enable --json","scenario":"one JSON document: `enabled` or `unchanged`"}]}

Usage: workspace work-queue disable [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]

Turn the workspace's queue off.

The running item keeps going and is still read by a pass; no new item starts.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace work-queue disable    # stop the queue from starting anything new
  workspace work-queue disable --name api.worktree-x    # the same for another workspace
  workspace work-queue disable --json    # one JSON document: `disabled` or `unchanged`

### workspace work-queue resume --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace work-queue resume [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]

Clear the queue's pause.

A failed or cancelled item pauses the queue. Resume changes only the pause; a held item is still held (see `work-queue skip`).

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace work-queue resume    # let the queue go on after a pause
  workspace work-queue resume --name api.worktree-x    # the same for another workspace
  workspace work-queue resume --json    # one JSON document: `resumed` or `unchanged`
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace work-queue skip --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace work-queue skip [ITEM] [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]

Skip the held item and clear the pause.

The held item goes to history as `skipped` and the queue resumes; its workflow run is left alone, and a warning
says so when it still goes and so blocks the next start (`workspace workflow cancel RUN` ends it).

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace work-queue skip    # give up on the held item and move on
  workspace work-queue skip 3fa9    # name the item
  workspace work-queue skip --json    # for a script: the row has the run id and a next action
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace work-queue advance --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace work-queue advance [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]

Run one pass of the queue by hand.

The pass reads the running item and finishes or holds it, or starts the next item when the queue is on, not
paused and no workflow run is going in the workspace. It works in the workspace's own checkout. Turn the queue
on first with `workspace work-queue enable`; an off queue starts nothing. Only this verb moves a queue, so run it
again after each item ends. Each thing the pass did is printed as a sentence; the exit code is 1 when the pass
hit a failure (a start that failed, a lost claim, an interrupted, failed or cancelled run), 3 when only some
rows did, and 0 when an item is just held at a gate.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace work-queue advance    # after `workspace work-queue enable`: start the next item
  workspace work-queue advance --name api.worktree-x    # one pass for another workspace
  workspace work-queue advance --json    # for a script: one row per thing the pass did
--- stderr
--- end

It works in the workspace's own checkout. Turn the queue\non first with `workspace work-queue enable`; an off queue starts nothing. Only this verb moves a queue, so run it\nagain after each item ends. Each thing the pass did is printed as a sentence; the exit code is 1 when the pass\nhit a failure (a start that failed, a lost claim, an interrupted, failed or cancelled run), 3 when only some\nrows did, and 0 when an item is just held at a gate.","options":[{"flags":"--name NAME","description":"Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)"},{"flags":"--json","description":"Print one JSON document"},{"flags":"-h, --help","description":"Show this help"}],"examples":[{"command":"workspace work-queue advance","scenario":"after `workspace work-queue enable`: start the next item"},{"command":"workspace work-queue advance --name api.worktree-x","scenario":"one pass for another workspace"},{"command":"workspace work-queue advance --json","scenario":"for a script: one row per thing the pass did"}]}

Usage: workspace work-queue status [--name WORKSPACE | --project [NAME]] [--json]

Show one line per queue: on or off, pause, active item.

The line says on, off or paused (and why), the active item and how many are queued.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)
    --project [NAME]             Every workspace of a project (NAME, or the project of the current workspace), read only
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace work-queue status    # the queue of the workspace you are in
  workspace work-queue status --project    # one line per workspace of the project
  workspace work-queue status --json    # one JSON document, with next actions

### workspace work-queue history list --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace work-queue history list [--since DATE] [--before DATE] [--state STATE] [--name WORKSPACE | --project [NAME]] [--json]

List finished items, oldest first.

DATE is 2026-01-31 or 2026-01-31T09:00:00Z.
STATE is one of succeeded, failed, cancelled, skipped, interrupted, launch_failed. History is kept for 365 days. --project reads and prunes nothing.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)
    --project [NAME]             Every workspace of a project (NAME, or the project of the current workspace), read only
    --since DATE                 Finished at or after this date
    --before DATE                Finished before this date
    --state STATE                Only this outcome
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace work-queue history list    # everything the queue finished
  workspace work-queue history list --state failed --since 2026-01-01    # the failures of this year
  workspace work-queue history list --project --json    # every workspace of the project, as one JSON document
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace work-queue history clear --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace work-queue history clear (--before DATE | --all) [--yes] [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]

Delete finished items.

DATE is 2026-01-31 or 2026-01-31T09:00:00Z.
Give exactly one of --before and --all. It asks first; --yes skips the question, and --json needs it.

Options:
    --name NAME                  Workspace (default: detected from the current directory)
    --before DATE                Delete items finished before this date
    --all                        Delete every finished item
    --yes                        Skip the question
    --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                   Show this help

Examples:
  workspace work-queue history clear --before 2026-01-01    # drop the old entries, after a question
  workspace work-queue history clear --all --yes    # empty the history with no question
  workspace work-queue history clear --all --yes --json    # for a script: one row with the count removed

### workspace work-queue
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace work-queue add workflow ID [--ref REF] [--prompt TEXT] [--input K=V]... [OPTIONS]
       workspace work-queue add go ARG [--text] [--workflow ID] [--input K=V]... [OPTIONS]
       workspace work-queue list [--name WORKSPACE | --project [NAME]] [--json]
       workspace work-queue show ITEM [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace work-queue active [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace work-queue rm ITEM... [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace work-queue move ITEM (--before ID | --after ID | --top | --bottom) [--if-revision N] [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace work-queue cancel [ITEM] [--and-continue] [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace work-queue enable [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace work-queue disable [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace work-queue resume [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace work-queue skip [ITEM] [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace work-queue advance [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace work-queue status [--name WORKSPACE | --project [NAME]] [--json]
       workspace work-queue history list [--since DATE] [--before DATE] [--state STATE] [--name WORKSPACE | --project [NAME]] [--json]
       workspace work-queue history show ITEM [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]
       workspace work-queue history clear (--before DATE | --all) [--yes] [--name WORKSPACE] [--json]

Each workspace has its own queue of items that run one at a time (`wq` is another name for
`work-queue`). A queue is off until `work-queue enable`. Only `work-queue advance` moves it, one
pass by hand, so run it again after each item ends.

Subcommands:
  add            Add an item to the end of a workspace's queue
  list           Show the queue as a table
  show           Show one queued item in full
  active         Show the item that is running and what it waits on
  rm             Remove queued items
  move           Move a queued item
  cancel         Cancel the running item and pause the queue
  enable         Turn the workspace's queue on
  disable        Turn the workspace's queue off
  resume         Clear the queue's pause
  skip           Skip the held item and clear the pause
  advance        Run one pass of the queue by hand
  status         Show one line per queue: on or off, pause, active item
  history list   List finished items, oldest first
  history show   Show one finished item with its spec
  history clear  Delete finished items
Run `workspace work-queue VERB --help` for a verb's options.

        --name NAME                  Workspace whose queue to use (default: detected from the current directory)
        --project [NAME]             list, status and history list: every workspace of a project (read only)
        --top                        add: put the item first among the queued ones; move: move it there
        --bottom                     move: move the item to the end
        --after-current              add: put the item right after the one that is running
        --before VALUE               add and move: place the item before this item id; history list and clear: finished before this date
        --after ID                   add and move: place the item after this item id
        --if-revision N              move: refuse with stale_revision unless the queue's revision is N
        --headless                   add: run the item without a pane
        --on-fail MODE               add: stop (pause the queue when it fails, the default) or continue
        --dedupe-key KEY             add: adding the same key again changes nothing
        --ref REF                    add workflow: the ticket, pull request or branch to start from
        --prompt TEXT                add workflow: the task text
        --input K=V                  add: a workflow input (repeatable)
        --text                       add go: ARG is free text, not a ticket, pull request or branch
        --workflow ID                add go: the workflow to run instead of the one config picks
        --and-continue               cancel: go on to the next item instead of pausing the queue
        --since DATE                 history list: finished at or after this date (2026-01-31 or 2026-01-31T09:00:00Z)
        --state STATE                history list: only this outcome (succeeded, failed, cancelled, skipped, interrupted, launch_failed)
        --all                        history clear: remove every finished item
        --yes                        history clear: skip the question
        --json                       Print one JSON document
    -h, --help                       Show this help

Examples:
  workspace work-queue add workflow rpiv --prompt "Add SSO login"    # queue an rpiv run for that task
  workspace work-queue list    # the queue of the workspace you are in
  workspace work-queue show 3fa9    # one item by the start of its id
  workspace work-queue active    # which item the queue is on, and what it waits for
  workspace work-queue rm 3fa9    # drop one queued item
  workspace work-queue move 3fa9 --top    # run this one next
  workspace work-queue cancel    # stop the running item and hold the queue
  workspace work-queue enable    # turn the queue on, then run `workspace work-queue advance`
--- stderr
--- end
